scope: Vulvar cancer is grounded in the 2023 ESGO guideline. Vaginal cancer is grounded in the open 2025 FIGO update.

keyRecommendations.text: FIGO staging of vulvar cancer was last reviewed in 2021. Ultrasound alone is the method of choice for preoperative assessment of clinically suspicious groin nodes.
Primary vaginal cancer is cancer in the vagina without clinical or histologic cervical or vulvar cancer, or a prior history of those cancers within 5 years.
Surgery has a limited role in primary vaginal cancer because of the close proximity of the tumor to adjacent structures.

clinicalBottomLine: Stage and assess vulvar cancer with the ESGO pathway, including ultrasound for suspicious groins. Call a vaginal lesion primary only after excluding cervix and vulva, and do not expect surgery to be the main treatment.
notableCaveats: The ESGO vaginal pocket PDF is not stored because it is not licensed for redistribution. The FIGO 2025 update is the open vaginal-cancer source.

source.title: European Society of Gynaecological Oncology guidelines for the management of patients with vulvar cancer - update 2023.
